title: Operator decision log — controlled degradation in eu-west-1
content:
Summary:

A partial edge degradation in eu-west-1 on 2025-02-13 produced sustained elevated p50/p95 latency for inference traffic and an increase in 5xx responses from edge proxies to origin. Client-observed errors climbed to ~12% for a~30-minute window for affected POPs. We performed a controlled degradation: reduced traffic weights to eu-west-1 while keeping warm-standby US-WEST able to accept additional capacity. Objective was to avoid mass DNS TTL churn and to preserve KV-cache warm state where possible.

Why this doc exists:
- Capture operator decisions made during incident to inform runbook updates
- Surface telemetry queries and decision criteria that actually proved useful
- Capture unresolved questions and follow-ups for infra and platform teams

Incident timeline (operator view):
- 05:12 UTC: Pager alert — global edge latency spike, localized to eu-west-1 client-facing POPs. Spike coincides with higher 5xx from edge->origin traces.
- 05:14: quick triage: edge health pages show elevated connection timeouts to origin cluster behind eu-west-1 LB. SRE on-call (Priya) escalates to infra and serving-runtime.
- 05:18: Begin runbook checks: confirm control-plane is healthy, model-runtime pods show no OOMs. KV-cache hit ratio drops ~8% in eu-west region (likely due to partial proxy flaps).
- 05:20: Decision point A — aggressive DNS failover vs weighted shift. Chosen: weighted shift (lower blast radius) because origin two-layer cache still usable and we wanted to preserve per-customer affinity/state.
- 05:22: Execute traffic weight reduction: reduce eu-west-1 route weight to 40% of baseline, increase us-west-2 weight to absorb 60% of requests. Applied routing change via traffic-manager API.
- 05:25: Observe immediate telemetry: p95 in eu-west drops slightly, overall 5xx falls from 12% -> 8%. Some clients still see errors due to DNS resolution to edge POPs with stale TTL.
- 05:30: Operator note: TTL for regional DNS entries was 180s; 2min of residual connection attempts caused transient retries and some 429s at edge.
- 05:35: Infra reports origin LB in eu-west recovered some connections but still showing elevated connection reset counts.
- 05:42: Decision point B — move to a staged DNS weight push to US-WEST but keep eu-west as warm for sticky traffic. Reduce eu-west weight to 15%, add US-EAST 20% to distribute load.
- 05:55: Latency and 5xx back to acceptable range (<2% 5xx). Begin monitoring for 45 minutes before rolling back weights.
- 06:40: Confirmed stability, start gradual normalization: ramp eu-west to 60% over 30 minutes, then to baseline after 2 hours.

Key operator decisions and rationale:
- Chose weighted routing adjustments instead of immediate DNS cutoff: avoids TTL churn, preserves KV cache warm state and reduces time-to-normal once origin stabilizes.
- Avoided immediate global failover because origin dependency was at proxy->origin layer and not a complete region outage; full failover would have incurred larger cold-cache cost and higher cost for customers using dedicated capacity.
- Coordinated small bursts to US-EAST in addition to US-WEST to avoid saturating a single standby region and to keep per-region latency within SLO for the most latency-sensitive customers.

Useful telemetry and quick queries used during triage (copypaste-ready):
- Edge -> origin 5xx count over 5m by POP: (metric query) edge.proxy.responses{pop:eu-west-*} | rate(5m) where code=5xx
- KV-cache hit ratio by region: serving.kvcache.hits / serving.kvcache.requests by region (rolling 1m)
- Client-experienced 4xx/5xx by region and API key: api.response.counts{region,api_key} | topk(20)
- DNS resolution TTL & active connection attempts to POPs: dns.query.counts{pop=eu-west-*} and active_conn_count for edge POPs
- Weighted routing state: traffic-manager.routes{route=hosted-api}.weights[eu-west-1,us-west-2,us-east-1]

Commands executed (for posterity):
- curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TM_TOKEN' -X POST https://traffic-manager.internal/api/v1/adjust-weight -d '{"route":"hosted-api","region":"eu-west-1","weight":0.4}'
- trafficctl get route hosted-api --json | jq '.weights'
- kubectl logs -n serving-runtime proxy-eu-west-*(last 2h) | grep "connection reset" | wc -l

What worked well:
- Having a pre-existing warm-standby footprint in two different US regions allowed traffic to be absorbed without triggering autoscale-induced cold starts everywhere.
- Traffic-manager API supported sub-minute weight changes and returned per-change audit IDs — made rollbacks traceable.
- Telemetry dashboard that correlates edge 5xx with origin TCP resets and KV-cache dropouts was crucial for fast root-cause hypothesis.

What didn't work / friction points:
- DNS TTLs: 180s TTL is longer than ideal for quick region surgery in some cases. Left residual traffic for ~2 minutes, causing small but noisy error tail.
- On-call playbook lacked a clear pre-approved policy for adding an extra standby region mid-incident (we used judgment; should be codified).
- Some runbook steps assume console access to a specific internal dashboard which was rate-limited during surge; need fallback query snippets in runbook.

Runbook changes proposed (short checklist):
- Add a section "Preferred immediate actions for partial POP-origin degradation" that pushes weighted routing first, then DNS adjustments only if weighted routing fails in N minutes.
- Lower regional DNS TTLs from 180s -> 60s for low-latency client-facing entries (with marketing and infra alignment on cache invalidation risk).
- Add explicit approval matrix for adding additional standby regions during incident (who can approve cost-bearing changes).
- Add a small appendix with the telemetry queries and 'trafficctl' examples above, plus a note about KV-cache re-warming time estimates per model size.

Unresolved questions / follow-ups (owners listed):
- (Infra) Why did origin LB experience connection resets? Follow-up JIRA created: JIRA-SRE-2374. Owner: Liang Chen.
- (Serving-runtime) Investigate why KV-cache hit ratio dropped before 5xx spike — causation or correlation? Owner: Marta Ruiz.
- (SRE) Re-evaluate global DNS TTL strategy for edge POP entries and coordinate with platform security and CDN partners. Owner: Priya Shah.
- (Cost) Estimate expected egress and compute delta for future incidents if we add a third standby region as a default. Owner: Finance liaison (TBD).

Quick operator tips (notes to self style):
- If the origin error is TCP-level resets (not HTTP 5xx from app), prefer weight shifts over DNS to avoid client-side retries hitting failed POPs.
- When reducing region weight, always add capacity to at least two standbys if available to prevent saturation spikes in single failover region.
- Keep a small list of trafficctl curl commands in the runbook to use when console is unresponsive.

Post-incident action items (tracked):
- [ ] Add queries and trafficctl snippets to runbook (owner: Priya) — due 2025-03-08
- [ ] Lower TTL experiment proposal doc (owner: Platform infra) — due 2025-03-15
- [ ] Kaizen retro session with infra/serving-runtime to troubleshoot origin resets (owner: Liang) — schedule week of 2025-03-03
- [ ] Update canary/fallback policy doc to include staged multi-standby option (owner: SRE) — due 2025-03-22

Appendix: small warm-cache math (rough)
- Typical KV-cache re-warm for medium model (~7B) per node ~ 3–6 minutes under normal request mix. If we move a 30% load to a cold region, expect a temporary p95 increase ~200–400ms until KV warms.
- Cost note: 1h of additional cross-region egress at scale ~ rough $Xk (finance to fill in) — weigh vs customer impact.

End of doc.

-- raw operator scratch: next time try 60s TTL in a lab first. Logged high-level decision rationale into SRE-incident-runbook for later inclusion.
